reasons: Deviation classification is correct: § 3.2 renews for a term equal to the previous term (so a multi-year initial term auto-renews multi-year, walk-away territory) and imposes a 90-day non-renewal notice, exceeding the fallback ceiling of 60 days; no uplift cap exists anywhere.

The redline reaches the preferred position with a coherent, self-contained rewrite: 12-month renewal term, 30-day exit notice, 60-day vendor reminder, and a lesser-of-CPI-or-3% uplift cap. The high changed-character ratio (0.693) is justified because the rule requires resetting renewal term, notice window and adding a cap.
The failed 'notice window ≤ 60 days' check is a regex artifact — the redline plainly states 'at least thirty (30) days prior', which satisfies the parametric ceiling.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook rationale and offers the 60-day / 5% fallback, as the redline guidance contemplates.

Minor, non-fatal notes for the drafter: (a) the mutual 30-day notice also lets the vendor exit on shorter notice than today's 90 days, so consider making the shortened window Customer-side only (preferred position is a Customer opt-out); (b) confirm 'IBM' is the defined counterparty name used elsewhere in the agreement before inserting it in the reminder sentence.
